summary: Concurrent model-warmup sweep + snapshotter I/O burst caused regional dedicated GPU attach drought and autoscaler undershoot
description:
Issue summary:
During a customer-observed midday window AtlasAI experienced a sustained drop in dedicated throughput (p50/p95) and an increase in 5xx attach errors for their pinned routes. Impact: customer saw ~40% throughput reduction for ~45 minutes and experienced timeouts on long poll sessions.

Impact:
- Guaranteed dedicated throughput degraded, client saw elevated error rates and long tail latencies.
- Customer business impact: degraded ingestion pipeline and slower feature responses.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated: reserved pool in us-east-1
- Customer: AtlasAI (dedicated tier, pinned model redwood/gptx-13b-v1)
- Time window: 2026-03-08 12:10 - 12:58 UTC

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer traffic steady (normal per-token distribution).
2) Simultaneous platform jobs: scheduled model-warmup sweep (kernel calibration + kv-cache priming) kicked off in the cluster and background snapshotter run started writing checkpoints to NVMe pool.
3) Within minutes we observed: rising snapshotter IO throughput, NVMe IO latency P95 spike, allocator heartbeat delay, increase in attach-timeouts to GPUs and autoscaler detecting apparent shortage -> scaled down some burst replicas.

Observed behavior:
- Autoscaler performed a transient shrink (cooldown) in the face of delayed attach acknowledgements.
- Several attach RPCs returned 5xx / timeout for ephemeral requests, leading to client retry storms and queued backlog.
- GPU attach latency distribution shifted to the right (p95->p999).

Expected behavior:
- Background maintenance jobs should not materially increase attach latency nor trigger autoscaler undershoot.

Relevant logs & dashboards:
- Allocator heartbeat traces: grafana.redwood/allocators/us-east/heatmap (link in comments)
- NVMe metrics: metrics.redwood/nvme/us-east/p95_io_ms
- Snapshotter job id: snapshotter-20260308-11:58 (joinable in logs)
comments: [2026-03-08 12:35 UTC] Support - Aisha Kapoor: Customer reported sustained p95 and p999 latency increase and a rise in 5xx for their dedicated pinned routes. Collected request/attach traces and forwarded to SRE. SLA opened as P1.

[2026-03-08 12:48 UTC] SRE - Priya Nair: Observed NVMe io latency spike coincident with snapshotter writes. Allocator heartbeats delayed by ~300-600ms and attach RPCs timing out. Posting traces: https://grafana.redwood/trace/abc123

[2026-03-08 13:05 UTC] Eng - Rafael Munoz: Autoscaler shrink appears to have been triggered after seeing repeated attach failures. Hypothesis: IO stall from snapshot writes causes attach ack latency -> autoscaler underestimates capacity and removes burst slots. Working on checkpoint: throttle snapshotter IO and monitor attach retries.

[2026-03-08 13:22 UTC] Support - Aisha Kapoor (to customer): Implemented temporary snapshotter IO rate limit in the affected region and bumped allocator attach timeout. Please validate client behavior.
investigation_notes: Timeline correlation: NVMe p95 spikes at 12:12 UTC; snapshotter bulk flush started at 12:10 UTC; warmup sweep (model shard kernel tuning) started at 12:09 UTC.
Allocator heartbeat delays observed on 6/12 allocator instances serving the reserved pool; heartbeat jitter correlated with RPC queue depth on the node.
Attach RPC traces show redwood-serving-runtime:Attach() spending time in kernel io wait and epoll wake delays before returning success/error.
Autoscaler logic evaluated replica health by attach ACK latency and dropped burst capacity as a protective step; due to delayed ACKs it mis-classified capacity as unhealthy.
Customer-specific config: AtlasAI has aggressive prewarm and long-lived streams which amplified attach retry storms when errors surfaced.

Cross-team note: background model-warmup jobs are co-located on host set that shares NVMe pool with dedicated cluster replicas; snapshotter retention churn coincided with warmup-induced prefetch writes.
Reproduced locally in staging with a synthetic workload that triggers concurrent warmup + checkpointing: attach p95 rose by ~4.6x and autoscaler shrank burst by 30% within 90s.
No evidence of underlying GPU driver crash or CUDA faults; errors are attach-timeout/5xx and IO latency related.
root_cause: A confluence of a scheduled model-warmup sweep (heavy kernel/cache priming) and a simultaneous snapshotter checkpoint flush saturated the shared NVMe IO subsystem on several nodes. NVMe IO latency increased, causing allocator heartbeat and attach RPCs to be delayed. The autoscaler interpreted delayed attach ACKs as unhealthy capacity and reduced burst replicas, producing an overall transient dedicated throughput shortfall. Customer-specific long-lived streams and retry behavior amplified queueing and visible impact.
mitigation_steps_taken: Applied immediate snapshotter IO rate limit in us-east-1 (throttle to 30% of previous peak) and scheduled checkpoint flushes with jitter.
Increased attach RPC timeouts temporarily to reduce false-negative health signals to autoscaler.
Pinned the model-warmup sweep to a reduced concurrency for the affected host group and moved heavy warmup jobs to maintenance window.
Manually triggered an autoscaler stabilization window and re-queued burst allocation to recover capacity.
Notified AtlasAI via support channel and requested confirmation of recovery metrics.
resolution_notes: 12:58 UTC - throughput returned to within 95% of baseline after snapshotter throttle and autoscaler stabilization window.
13:10 UTC - confirmed no persistent GPU attach failures; customer validated reduced error rate and resumed normal traffic patterns.
Follow-up: scheduled a post-incident review with runtime, scheduler, and storage teams to define long-term controls.
action_items: (ENG) Add NVMe IO headroom checks to autoscaler health signals to avoid misclassification from transient IO stalls - owner: Rafael Munoz - due: 2026-03-22
(SRE) Introduce snapshotter scheduling jitter and per-tenant IO capping for dedicated host pools - owner: Priya Nair - due: 2026-03-15
(Product) Add advisory to customers about long-lived streams and retry backoff best practices for dedicated pools - owner: Claire Zhang - due: 2026-03-18
(Support) Reach out to AtlasAI with RCA and recommended client retry/backoff tuning - owner: Aisha Kapoor - due: 2026-03-12
follow_up_notes: RCA meeting scheduled 2026-03-12 16:00 UTC with runtime, storage, autoscaler teams.
Consider long-term: introduce a storage-tier QoS or isolation for dedicated host NVMe to prevent co-located maintenance impacting attach latency.
